exams.name: Initial
lists: Learn as You Play Tuned Percussion & Timpani
Play Drum Kit, Timpani & Percussion book 1
exams.syllabus: Trinity Drum Kit & Percussion syllabus. Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Face-to-face: Initial-G5: 3 pieces/studies 22 each (66; each piece = fluency & accuracy 7 + technical facility 7 + communication & interpretation 8), technical work 14, two supporting tests 10 each (20) = 100. G6-8: same but supporting test 1 = sight reading (10) and test 2 = aural/unpitched aural (drum kit only)/improvisation (10). Digital technical-work pathway: 3 pieces 22 each (66) + technical work 14 + overall performance 20 (delivery & focus 10, musical awareness 10) = 100; no supporting tests. Digital repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces/studies at 25 each = 100. Attainment: Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44 (per piece: D 19-22, M 16-18, P 13-15). No need to pass every section. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (pass/merit/distinction).

Drum kit: 3 pieces, two from group A (played with Trinity backing track, with or without click) and one from group B (unaccompanied, no click/headphones); max one from Raise the Bar Drum Kit at G1-8; own composition may replace group B piece. Orchestral percussion (combined exam): 3 pieces, one each from tuned percussion, snare drum and timpani lists (no studies); at least one accompanied piece to G5; own composition may replace one. Tuned percussion: 2 pieces + 1 study (digital repertoire-only: 3 pieces + 1 study); at least one accompanied piece to G5; two mallets to G5, G6-8 mallet number marked in list; own composition may replace a piece. Snare drum: 2 pieces + 1 rudimental study (repertoire-only: 3 + 1); at least one accompanied piece to G3. Timpani: 2 pieces + 1 study (repertoire-only: 3 + 1); accompanied piece required to G5; two drums to G3, G4-8 drums marked in list. Repeats: drum kit observe all; other instruments observe repeats of 4 bars or fewer only. Face-to-face accompaniment must be live from G4 for percussion (recorded allowed to G3, candidate supplies equipment); examiner operates drum kit backing tracks. Own compositions: durations Initial 0.5-1 min rising to G8 3.5-5 min; stave notation required G6-8; not marked on compositional quality.

Digital exams (filmed, one continuous take, max 3GB, uploaded via Trinity portal) offer two pathways: Technical work pathway (3 pieces + technical work + overall performance, no supporting tests) or Repertoire-only pathway (4 pieces, 25 marks each). Digital technical work: exercises (any two of the three listed, not examiner-chosen), tuned percussion scales as Set A or Set B (from memory), snare orchestral figures Set A or B, orchestral extracts G6-8 (two chosen from three). Recorded accompaniment permitted at all grades in digital exams; no headphones/click for technical work or unaccompanied pieces; electric kit allowed to G5 face-to-face.
sections: Scales & technical work

Exercises (all three at trinitycollege.com/percussion-tw; music may be used): sticking patterns, roll development, dynamics. Face-to-face: prepare all, candidate chooses one, examiner one of remaining; digital: play any two. Two mallets.
Sight-reading
Unseen test, 30 s prep, one level below grade: C major, 4/4, f, minims/crotchets/quavers, crotchet rest. Face-to-face only; may be played on tuned percussion, snare or timpani in combined exam.
Aural & other tests

Choose any two of: sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge (10 marks each). Musical knowledge: pitch names, note durations, clefs/staves/bar lines, key and time signatures, basic terms. Aural (piano): 4-bar major melody on piano: clap pulse on 3rd hearing; f or p; legato or staccato; highest or lowest of first three notes. Improvisation: choose stylistic (over examiner's piano part, 2-bar intro), motivic (response to 1-2 bar fragment) or harmonic (chord sequence) stimulus; 30 s prep to G5.

sections: Scales & technical work

Scales & arpeggios from memory, one octave, hand to hand, mf. Face-to-face (examiner selects): C, G, F major; A, E, D minor (harmonic/melodic/natural); chromatic from C; scales min minim=70; arpeggios C, G, F major and A, E, D minor, min crotchet=100. Digital Set A: C major, A minor, chromatic on C, arpeggios G major, D minor; Set B: F major, E minor, chromatic on C, arpeggios C major, A minor.
Sight-reading
Cumulative: tuned perc/timpani add G and F major, A minor; adds 2/4, 3/4, p and mf. Face-to-face only; may be played on tuned percussion, snare or timpani in combined exam.
Aural & other tests

Choose any two of: sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge (10 marks each). Musical knowledge: note values, key/time signatures, ledger-line notes (to 2), terms/signs. Aural (piano): 4-bar major melody: clap pulse (3rd hearing); f/p and legato/staccato; last note higher/lower than first; spot where a rhythm or pitch change occurs. Improvisation: choose stylistic (over examiner's piano part, 2-bar intro), motivic (response to 1-2 bar fragment) or harmonic (chord sequence) stimulus; 30 s prep to G5.

Either (1) scales & arpeggios from memory, min minim=60 (arpeggios 60, 7ths 100), mf: major scales two octaves hand to hand or in 3rds, major one octave legato roll or in octaves, melodic and harmonic minors, chromatic in minor 3rds; arpeggio/broken chord two octaves; dom 7th and dim 7th. F2F: F, G major; D, E minors; chromatic in minor 3rds on F, D; dim 7th C#, E, G, Bb. Digital Set A: F major, G major, D melodic minor, E harmonic minor, chromatic minor 3rds from F, arpeggios G major broken chord, E minor, dom 7th G, dim 7th C#; Set B: G, F, E melodic, D harmonic, chromatic from D, F major broken chord, D minor, dom 7th F, dim 7th Bb. Or (2) orchestral extracts: Britten Young Person's Guide Var. M; Copland Rodeo Hoe-Down; Tchaikovsky Sleeping Beauty Waltz (F2F: prepare all three, candidate picks one, examiner one; digital: choose two). Four-octave instrument required G6-8.
Sight-reading
Adds E major, C/F minor, 5/4, fz, two-note chords (tuned). Face-to-face only; may be played on tuned percussion, snare or timpani in combined exam.
Aural & other tests

Sight reading (10) plus one of aural / improvisation (10). Aural (piano): 8-bar harmonised major piece: time signature, dynamics, articulation, two other characteristics; modulation (subdominant/dominant/relative minor); with copy locate two melody changes (pitch/rhythm). Improvisation: choose stylistic (over examiner's piano part, 2-bar intro), motivic (response to 1-2 bar fragment) or harmonic (chord sequence) stimulus; 30 s prep to G5.

comps: Face-to-face: Initial-G5: 3 pieces/studies 22 each (66; each piece = fluency & accuracy 7 + technical facility 7 + communication & interpretation 8), technical work 14, two supporting tests 10 each (20) = 100. G6-8: same but supporting test 1 = sight reading (10) and test 2 = aural/unpitched aural (drum kit only)/improvisation (10). Digital technical-work pathway: 3 pieces 22 each (66) + technical work 14 + overall performance 20 (delivery & focus 10, musical awareness 10) = 100; no supporting tests. Digital repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces/studies at 25 each = 100. Attainment: Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44 (per piece: D 19-22, M 16-18, P 13-15). No need to pass every section. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (pass/merit/distinction).

Drum kit: 3 pieces, two from group A (played with Trinity backing track, with or without click) and one from group B (unaccompanied, no click/headphones); max one from Raise the Bar Drum Kit at G1-8; own composition may replace group B piece. Orchestral percussion (combined exam): 3 pieces, one each from tuned percussion, snare drum and timpani lists (no studies); at least one accompanied piece to G5; own composition may replace one. Tuned percussion: 2 pieces + 1 study (digital repertoire-only: 3 pieces + 1 study); at least one accompanied piece to G5; two mallets to G5, G6-8 mallet number marked in list; own composition may replace a piece. Snare drum: 2 pieces + 1 rudimental study (repertoire-only: 3 + 1); at least one accompanied piece to G3. Timpani: 2 pieces + 1 study (repertoire-only: 3 + 1); accompanied piece required to G5; two drums to G3, G4-8 drums marked in list. Repeats: drum kit observe all; other instruments observe repeats of 4 bars or fewer only. Face-to-face accompaniment must be live from G4 for percussion (recorded allowed to G3, candidate supplies equipment); examiner operates drum kit backing tracks. Own compositions: durations Initial 0.5-1 min rising to G8 3.5-5 min; stave notation required G6-8; not marked on compositional quality.
None. No theory or lower-grade prerequisite for any grade; grades assume confidence in earlier requirements.

Digital exams (filmed, one continuous take, max 3GB, uploaded via Trinity portal) offer two pathways: Technical work pathway (3 pieces + technical work + overall performance, no supporting tests) or Repertoire-only pathway (4 pieces, 25 marks each). Digital technical work: exercises (any two of the three listed, not examiner-chosen), tuned percussion scales as Set A or Set B (from memory), snare orchestral figures Set A or B, orchestral extracts G6-8 (two chosen from three). Recorded accompaniment permitted at all grades in digital exams; no headphones/click for technical work or unaccompanied pieces; electric kit allowed to G5 face-to-face.

Houllif: American percussion composer of solo and ensemble works.
Glennie: Scottish solo percussionist and composer, famed for marimba performances.
Berg: Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School who combined twelve-tone technique with intense Romantic expression.
Pitfield: English composer, teacher and writer known for approachable, witty instrumental pieces.
Weyer: Composer of marimba pieces in Spinning Yarns.
Trad., arr. Glennie: Traditional Irish melody arranged by Evelyn Glennie.
Menken: American composer of Disney film musicals including The Little Mermaid, Aladdin and Pocahontas.
Goldenberg: American percussionist who wrote the Modern School for Snare Drum.
Rosauro: Brazilian percussionist and composer, best known for his Marimba Concerto No. 1.
Humperdink, arr. Pimentel & Moore: German late-Romantic composer, best known for the opera Hänsel und Gretel.
Aldous: British percussion educator and composer of tuned percussion and drum kit teaching pieces.
Zivkovic: Serbian-German percussionist and composer, known for marimba works.
Mead: Composer of the xylophone piece Roller-Coaster.
Offenbach, arr. Alan: German-born French composer of operettas, creator of the can-can in Orpheus in the Underworld.
Bernstein, arr. O'Reilly: American composer and conductor, best known for West Side Story; arranged by John O'Reilly.
Steinquest: Composer of the xylophone piece Rudimental Ragtime.
Barratt: Contemporary composer or arranger of graded teaching music for wind instruments.
Barry: Composer of a concerto for baritone.
Mayuzumi: Japanese avant-garde composer, known for Nirvana Symphony and the Xylophone Concertino.
Inns: Composer of the marimba piece Robbin' Harry.
Berenska: Composer of the marimba piece Taps in Tempo.
Elings: Composer of swing-style pieces for tuned percussion.
Garraway: Composer of educational snare drum pieces.
Ptasazyńska: Polish composer and percussionist, known for works for percussion.
Brice: Composer of the marimba piece Valiseeh.
Hext: Composer of educational pieces for tuned percussion and timpani.
Aldous, Evans & Pearcey: Trinity percussion team writing educational ensemble pieces for the exam syllabus.
Musser: American marimbist, composer and instrument designer.
Faulkner: Composer of beginner double bass pieces in the First Bass and Second Bass collections published by Recital Music.
Peters: American percussionist and composer of well-known marimba and timpani repertoire.
Merkies: Composer of pop-rock blues pieces for tuned percussion.
van Gorp: Composer of Big Swing Pop pieces for tuned percussion.
Alford: British military bandmaster, composer of Colonel Bogey and other famous marches.
Dittersdorf, arr. Boo: Classical-period Austrian composer, contemporary of Haydn and Mozart.
Pearcey: Composer of Trinity percussion studies and pieces.
Gomez: Composer of marimba solos including Marimba Flamenca.
Butov: Russian composer and marimbist, author of 24 Etudes for Marimba.
Newman: American singer-songwriter and film composer, known for Pixar scores.
Lipner: Composer of the mallet piece Crystal Mallet.
